Spreadsheets are great for **storing** data and **looking up** a single value. They are terrible for **seeing patterns**. Our eyes and brains can only hold a handful of numbers at a time, but they can take in the shape of thousands of points at a glance.

Each page on this site runs the same little experiment:

1. **The spreadsheet.** You get the raw data, just like you'd receive it in a CSV.
2. **Your guess.** A question about the data. Try to answer it by scanning the table. Give yourself a minute (really!).
3. **The reveal.** Open the chart and see how long the same answer takes.

## The experiments

| Page | Charts | The hidden pattern is about… |
|---|---|---|
| [Histograms & Pie Charts](distributions.qmd) | histogram, pie chart | the **shape** of one variable and **parts of a whole** |
| [Bar Charts & Boxplots](groups.qmd) | bar chart, multi-boxplot | **comparing groups**, and why averages can lie |
| [Scatterplots](relationships.qmd) | scatterplot | the **relationship** between two numeric variables |
| [Lines Over Time](time.qmd) | grouped line plot | **trends, seasons, and sudden changes** over time |

::: {.callout-note}
## Every chart shows its code
Click **"Show the Python code"** above any chart to see exactly how it was made with `pandas`, `matplotlib`, and `seaborn`. The data are simulated in [`sim_data.py`](sim_data.py) with a fixed random seed, so everyone sees the same numbers.
:::
